newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya alliance set to resume "mass action" in days.
newsitem.headline: Kenya alliance set to resume "mass action" in days.

text.p: An alliance of opposition-backed groups demanding constitutional reforms in Kenya warned on Thursday it would resume "mass action" after August 21 if the government failed to start all-party reform talks by then.

The National Convention Executive Council (NCEC) -- an umbrella group of opposition parties, clerics, human rights groups and lawyers -- suspended mass rallies and demonstrations on Monday, three days after four people were killed in political violence.

The opposition wants President Daniel arap Moi, 73 and in power for 19 years, to enact constitutional reforms before presidential and parliamentary elections due later this year. No date has been set for the polls.

"The NCEC suspended, not cancelled mass action. If dialogue would not have started after that period (of 10 days), then we will review and decide what actions to take. We would resume mass action," senior NCEC official Kivutha Kibwana told a news conference.

But there appeared to be a disagreement over what form the action would take -- a paragraph in the official text of the NCEC statement announcing "the mother of all public rallies in independent Kenya" at Nairobi's Uhuru Park on August 23 was crossed out. The NCEC gave no explanation.

Another NCEC official, Willy Mutunga, said that political parties had agreed on a team of 50 people to negotiate for reforms under a group of religious leaders led by Anglican Archbishop David Gitari.
Kibwana said NCEC conditions for dialogue included Moi naming a team to negotiate and the government implementing a set of "minimum" reforms before the elections.
An NCEC statement read by Kibwana said more than 500 people had been arrested by police and charged with various offences since the NCEC launched its campaign for reforms on May 31.

"The government's strategy of indiscriminate arrest of pro-democracy activists and ordinary citizens is meant to intimidate Kenyans so that they desist from participating in peaceful mass civil action," the statement said.
"We call upon the government to stop criminalising the pro-democracy orientation of the mass of the Kenyan citizenry."
The NCEC was widely criticised by government officials and newspapers over the killing of the two policemen during a general strike last Friday called by the NCEC.
In the Indian Ocean port city of Mombasa, police said on Thursday six officers and seven civilians were killed when assailants burned down a police station, releasing prisoners and stealing firearms.

The motive for the Wednesday night attack, close to Kenya's favourite tourist beaches, was unclear. Some witnesses said the attackers were local people taking reprisals against Likoni police for alleged brutality.

Parliamentary opposition leader Michael Wamalwa and opposition FORD-Asili party chairman Kenneth Matiba have previously argued that the NCEC had no authority to negotiate on their behalf. Kibwana said the two were now on board.
Kibwana said NCEC negotiators would meet the mediating church group on Tuesday and that they had proposed the first session of "dialogue" on constitutional changes be held on August 21.
Kibwana said the NCEC also wanted the government to withdraw two bills it published on reforms because they were drafted without consultations with NCEC legal experts.
The NCEC also wanted the government to suspend all preparations for elections until after the successful completion of the constitutional reform talks.
The NCEC said it had heard rumours that Moi planned to dissolve parliament on August 28 and call for elections thereafter. It said the move would be "ill-advised".
Moi's government has come under renewed pressure from the International Monetary Fund, which halted a key aid package on July 31 because of concern at high-level corruption in Kenya.
The World Bank has delayed paying part of a loan to Kenya and said it would find it hard to hand over money until the government addressed corruption concerns.
